text: Continue the "one prop = one file" prop refactor (reqs req_0846 req_0848 req_0869 + close out req_0841/0849). RULING: the file with the most data about a prop owns ALL of it — each prop's registry def lives in its OWN geometry file (compile/propRecipes/<prop>.ts exports <name>Def: PropKindDefinition + <name>Parts()), and game/kinds/props.ts is just the ASSEMBLER that imports each <name>Def into PROP_KIND_DEFINITIONS. Mechanism already proven on the 4 chairs (commit cca2d6657). Remaining batches, each a green checkpoint (esbuild bundle props.ts + resolve.ts must stay green; commit explicit paths only, never git add -A; cite the req): (1) migrate the remaining ~60 prop defs out of PROP_KIND_DEFINITIONS in props.ts into their per-prop files the same way as chairs — geometry file gains `export const <name>Def: PropKindDefinition = {...}` (moved verbatim), reads its own local def for any scaling instead of propKindDefinition(kind), and props.ts replaces the inline entry with `<name>: <name>Def,` + the import. Keep the PropKind union hand-written. Do ~8-12 props per iteration, grouped. (2) After props.ts holds zero inline per-prop defs, rewrite the original ~30 declarative solo files (the ones using ./types lowerPropRecipe) into the builder form (box/cylinder8/cylinder16/sphere/panel/glassBox → PropPartSpec[]) and delete types.ts. (3) Fold streetSign into a recipe (add defaultTextureKey/texturedFaces to PropPartSpec + DataProp + the bake) and delete render3d/props/StreetSign.tsx. Each loop iteration: run `git log --oneline -5` to see what landed, grep props.ts for remaining inline defs (`grep -nE '^  [a-zA-Z]+: \{' cart/hmsc-int/game/kinds/props.ts`), then do the next batch. When a whole sub-piece (all defs migrated / all declarative files rewritten / streetSign folded) is fully done, move its req to review with a real paragraph + shas. Watch for import cycles (prop files import the PropKindDefinition TYPE only from props.ts; propModels stays pure kit). If something is genuinely ambiguous or blocked, say so and stop rather than guess.
